title: A Slack channel message claims a PR shipped that isn't merged
author: kothar-wa-khasis
description: The Slack source's third and final claims-X leg, alongside slack-message-claims-unfixed-issue (task 599) and slack-message-claims-open-milestone (task 601) -- that second recipe's own docstring named this exact leg as its own future seam before anyone built it. Also the Slack-side twin of linear-comment-claims-unmerged-pr (task 603), which closed the identical PR-claim leg for the Linear issue-comment surface and named this recipe as the claims-X grid's one remaining genuinely open cell. Extracts every 'ships/includes/merges/via #N' claim phrase (seam_engine.pr_claims' shared grammar, imported verbatim, the eighth recipe to bind to it) from a Slack channel message's own text and cross-checks it against the live PR tracker's own state. A PR that exists but is not merged is the seam: a message already sitting in a Slack channel disagrees with GitHub's own record, and nothing on either platform ever compares them. With this recipe shipped, the claims-X grid (ten sources times three targets) has zero genuinely open cells left. Fixture-only, MOCK ONLY, never a live network call -- the-hand gateway holds a real, connected upstream Slack app but exposes zero Slack-capable tools on its live toolset today, the same WIP note both of this recipe's own Slack siblings already carry. Neither scope is new (SearchChannelMessages and ListPullRequests are both already registered) and slack+github is not a new toolkit pair (both Slack siblings already proposed it).
confidence_notes: Age-gated by hours since the message's own created_at, holding slack-message-claims-open-milestone's/linear-comment-claims-unmerged-pr's own 0.85/0.5 bar exactly -- NOT review-comment-claims-unmerged-pr's lower 0.55/0.85 bar for an editable surface. A Slack channel message is posted once and stands, exactly as durable and readable-later as a Linear issue comment, a tweet, or a mention once posted -- mention-claims-unmerged-pr's/linear-comment-claims-unmerged-pr's identical bar applies, not review-comment-claims-unmerged-pr's bar, which exists because a review comment can be edited after posting; a Slack channel message cannot be un-said the same way. A claim checked within 24 hours of posting might still be a race (the PR actually merging moments after the message went out) rather than a settled public overclaim (0.5, below the 0.70 confidence bar, shown as a weighed-and-dropped coincidence, not hidden). At or past 24 hours with the named PR still unmerged, it is unambiguous (flat 0.85). The check itself is objective: the claimed PR's own live merged/state fields, verified against ListPullRequests, not a guess about which tracker the poster meant. A named PR that does not exist at all is excluded at confidence 0.0, named not hidden -- a broken reference is a future Slack-side dangling-reference recipe's own seam, not this one's. A named PR that IS merged is excluded too -- the claim was simply true. A message with no ships/includes/merges/via claim phrase at all produces no candidate. No text in this recipe's own headline/detail strings ever names or grades the Slack poster -- CONTRIBUTING.md's 'No grading, ever' law, same as every recipe in this engine.
